models.name: Gemma 4 E2B
models.summary: Fast and writes well in many languages, Russian included: about 27 words per second on iPhone 16. The best place to start.

models.name: Gemma 4 E4B
models.summary: Larger and more thoughtful, but slower: about 15 words per second on iPhone 16. Needs a phone with 8 GB of memory.

models.name: Qwen 3.5 4B
models.summary: About 15 words per second on iPhone 16. Noticeably weaker than Gemma in Russian in our tests.

models.name: QVikhr 3 4B
models.summary: Qwen 3 retrained for Russian by the Vikhr team: writes natural Russian and calls checks reliably. In our tests it sometimes misread numbers (it called a strong signal weak). Not yet measured on iPhone.

models.name: Ministral 3 3B
models.summary: Mistral's small model: good at calling checks and fairly fluent in Russian, although Russian is not officially supported. Tends to answer at length. Not yet measured on iPhone.

models.name: LFM3 1.7B
models.summary: The lightest and fastest (about 42 words per second), good for older phones. Its Russian is clumsy.

models.name: Llama 3.2 3B Abliterated
models.summary: A version of Llama 3.2 with its built-in refusals removed: it answers what ordinary models decline. About 24 tokens per second on iPhone 16. Russian is not officially supported: it writes it clumsily and slips into English words, so it suits English better.
models.notice: Built with Llama. The model's safety limits have been removed: it may give inaccurate, rude or inappropriate answers. Use at your own risk; not for children.

models.name: EmbeddingGemma 300M
models.summary: Not for chatting: it helps the web search find the right parts of pages by meaning, not only by matching words. In our trials it found the answer in all 16 cases, against 14 for matching words alone. Needs web search turned on.
